all_target_variables: Positive affect | Negative affect | Life satisfaction | Meaning in life | School belonging

title: Students' and schools' expectancy-value beliefs are associated with reading achievement: A cross-cultural study
authors: Jiajing Li, Ronnel B. King, Yi Wang, Wang Chuang, Shing On Leung
outcome_summary: This study conducts a secondary analysis of PISA 2018 reading literacy for 15-year-olds, comparing Eastern cultures (Mainland China, Hong Kong SAR, Macau SAR, Taiwan, South Korea, Japan; n = 41,872) and Western cultures (USA, UK, Canada, New Zealand, Australia; n = 61,755). Expectancy is operationalized as reading self-concept and value as intrinsic value, both modeled with a two-factor measurement structure and tested for measurement invariance across 11 countries and across student vs school levels. Reading achievement is modeled using all 10 plausible values, estimated ten times and combined using Rubin’s method. Using doubly-latent multilevel structural equation modeling, student-level expectancy and value show positive associations with reading achievement in both cultures (Eastern β = 0.33/0.29; Western β = 0.41/0.36), while school-level expectancy/value are significant only in the East (β = 0.25/0.18) and not in the West (β = 0.02/−0.008). The study uses MCMC imputation for missing items and applies final student weights; however, the cross-sectional PISA design limits causal interpretation.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2018 Reading literacy (15-year-olds), Eastern cultures (CHN, HKG, MAC, TWN, KOR, JPN) | PISA 2018 Reading literacy (15-year-olds), Western cultures (USA, GBR, CAN, NZL, AUS) | PISA 2018 Reading literacy (15-year-olds), cross-cultural multi-group comparison (Eastern vs Western)
all_target_variables: Reading achievement (Plausible Values) | Cross-cultural differences in expectancy/value paths to reading achievement

title: Female students and students from more affluent families benefit more from fear of failure in learning achievements: A study based on 77 economies
authors: Yuyang Cai, Zheng Jiang
outcome_summary: This cross-sectional study uses PISA 2018 student microdata from 77 economies to examine whether fear of failure predicts achievement in reading, mathematics, and science, and whether socioeconomic status (ESCS) and gender moderate these relationships. Achievement is modeled using PISA plausible values, with the authors using only the first plausible value per domain, and fear of failure is measured via three 4-point items (ST183Q01 and ST183Q02 items). The analysis is multilevel structural equation modelling (ML-SEM) with latent interactions (LMS) estimated in Mplus, reporting strong model fit for the baseline model (e.g., RMSEA=0.021, CFI=0.999, TLI=0.997) and significant improvement when adding interactions (ΔG2/df=252.80, p<.001). Fear of failure shows positive associations with all three achievements (β≈0.05–0.07, p<.001), while SES strengthens these effects and gender suppresses them (gender×fear interactions negative, p<.001). Limitations include the absence of explicit design-weight usage reporting and the inability to establish causal effects from cross-sectional data.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2018 (77 economies) Mathematics achievement (single plausible value) | PISA 2018 (77 economies) Reading achievement (single plausible value) | PISA 2018 (77 economies) Science achievement (single plausible value)
all_target_variables: Mathematics achievement (PISA 2018 PV) | Reading achievement (PISA 2018 PV) | Science achievement (PISA 2018 PV)

title: The issue of test-taking motivation in low- and high-stakes tests: are students underachieving in PISA?
authors: Linda Borger, Hanna Eklöf, Stefan Johansson, Rolf Strietholt
outcome_summary: The study links Swedish PISA 2018 reading outcomes (Grade 9; PISA reading achievement scored via 10 plausible values) with students’ grade 9 national reading test grades (high-stakes proxy for ability) and uses a latent-variable moderation framework to test whether self-reported test-taking effort (PISA TTE) predicts PISA performance beyond ability. In the main model, NT_Read strongly predicts PISA reading achievement (β=0.65, p<.001), while TTE shows a weaker but significant positive effect after controlling for NT_Read (β=0.15, p<.001). The moderation is statistically significant: the interaction TTE×NT_Read is positive (b=3.73, β=0.05, p<.001), with a small effect size (f2=0.005) and a modest R2 increase from 0.443 to 0.446. The paper applies student final weights (W_FSTUWT) and uses FIML for missingness, but it is not an ML predictive-modeling study and causal claims are limited by the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported effort.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2018 Grade 9 Reading (Sweden) with linked Grade 9 national reading test

title: Students’ reading enjoyment as a multilevel mediator of the relationship between parental reading enjoyment, teachers’ stimulation of reading, ICT factors, and reading literacy
authors: Sojin Yoon, JiYoon Kim, Sehee Hong
outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2018 reading literacy data for South Korea (6,650 students from 188 schools) and estimates a multilevel structural equation model (MSEM) to test how reading enjoyment mediates relationships among parental, teacher, and ICT-related factors. Reading literacy is modeled using the ten PISA plausible values, and the analysis applies PISA sampling weights to address the complex sampling design. At the student level, parents’ reading enjoyment and students’ reading enjoyment are positively associated with reading literacy (e.g., SER→Reading literacy B=42.753, p<.001), while students’ ICT interest is negatively associated with reading enjoyment (ICT interest→SER B=-0.119, p<.001) and shows a significant direct association with reading literacy (ICT interest→Reading literacy B=36.109, p<.001). At the school level, teachers’ stimulation of reading increases reading enjoyment (TSR→SER B=0.144, p<.001) and enjoyment predicts reading literacy (SER→Reading literacy B=346.304, p=.005), whereas schools’ ICT capacity has a significant negative direct effect on reading literacy (B=-16.064, p=.015). Limitations include cross-sectional mediation (no long-term causal inference) and the absence of ML predictive modeling despite the paper’s ML-related framing in the introduction.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2018 Reading literacy (South Korea, student level) | PISA 2018 Reading literacy (South Korea, school level)

title: Examining student ICT use and learning outcomes: Evidence from Japanese PISA data
outcome_summary: This study analyzes Japanese PISA 2018 microdata (15-year-olds; Japan only) to examine how five forms of student ICT use relate to reading, mathematics, and science achievement. The authors estimate 15 PV-based regression models using the R package intsvy, which accounts for PISA’s complex design via replicate weights and uses all plausible values for each domain; they also run unconditional quantile regression (UQR) using the first plausible value to assess heterogeneity across the achievement distribution. Across mean results, ICT use for leisure outside school is consistently negatively associated with all three outcomes, while subject-related ICT use during and outside lessons is positively associated with all three outcomes. Interaction results show that the direction/magnitude of associations varies by perceived ICT competence, and quantile results indicate stronger effects at distribution tails for some ICT-use forms. Limitations include cross-sectional (correlational) design and listwise deletion for missing data within the intsvy workflow.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2018 (Japan) Reading literacy | PISA 2018 (Japan) Mathematics literacy | PISA 2018 (Japan) Science literacy
all_target_variables: Reading achievement (PVs) | Mathematics achievement (PVs) | Science achievement (PVs)

title: Mind the gap: Examining migrant-native disparities in reading performance and subjective wellbeing among 15-year-old students in different education systems
authors: Z. Wang
outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 microdata for 15-year-olds from a subset of 15 countries, examining migrant-native disparities in reading performance and subjective wellbeing (happiness and life satisfaction). Reading is modeled using the mean of 10 plausible values, and the paper estimates multilinear regression models for the full sample and for four education-system clusters (early tracking; common core–uniform; common core–flexible; individualised). Across the full sample, migration background is associated with a 12.82-point lower reading score and a -0.077 lower life satisfaction score after controls, while its association with happiness is small and only weakly significant. Model fit is reported via R-squared (e.g., 0.280 for reading in Model 2). The analysis does not document survey-weight or missing-data handling, and the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation, so results should be treated as associations rather than causal effects.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2018 Reading (15-year-olds) — reading literacy (10 PV average) | PISA 2018 Subjective wellbeing (15-year-olds) — happiness (1–4 scale) | PISA 2018 Subjective wellbeing (15-year-olds) — life satisfaction (rescaled to 1–4)
all_target_variables: Reading performance (mean of 10 plausible values) | Happiness | Life satisfaction

title: Technology policy, technology integration, and equitable learning experiences: Insights in technological preparedness of US public schools for the pandemic
authors: Praveen K. Dubey
outcome_summary: This paper is a review-article style write-up (as labeled in the manuscript header) that uses PISA 2018 US questionnaire data (N=4,838; 162 schools) to model “technological preparedness” via a latent-variable approach. The authors do not train machine-learning predictive models; instead, they estimate a parcel-level CFA/SEM measurement model with ten constructs spanning school technology capacity/policy/capacity for learning, teacher technology utility/digital reading activity, and student technology availability/digital device use for learning/time spent/experience. They report measurement quality (e.g., construct reliability via omega) and test gender measurement invariance, latent mean/variance differences, and latent regressions for school location (rural to large city) and teacher gender. They explicitly state that PISA measure weights were not used because the analysis relies on perception data and does not use plausible values, and it does not compare across countries. Limitations include unclear missing-data handling and the fact that SEM-based associations are not causal estimates.

title: Education 5.0 challenges and sustainable development goals in emerging economies: A mixed-method approach
authors: V. Agarwal, Palak Verma, G. Ferrigno
outcome_summary: This paper is a mixed-methods study focused on identifying and prioritizing challenges to implementing Education 5.0 in an emerging economy context (India). It does not use ILSA student achievement data (no PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS microdata, no plausible values, and no predictive modeling of student outcomes). In Phase 1, the authors conducted semi-structured interviews with 14 academicians and used thematic analysis (NVIVO) to derive eight challenge dimensions. In Phase 2, they applied the Best-Worst Method (BWM) using inputs from 9 experts to compute decision-analytic weights and ranks, reporting a consistency ratio of 0.01392 and identifying Technology-based challenges (TBC) as the most critical and Student-Teacher Involvement challenges (STC) as the least critical. The main limitation is that the “weights” reflect expert prioritization rather than statistically estimated effects on educational outcomes, and the study does not provide ML performance metrics or survey-weighted inference.

title: Social and emotional skills and young people's expectations of social status and mobility
authors: Francesca Borgonovi, Seong Won Han
outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata for 205,231 15-year-old students in 27 countries that administered both the expected relative social status ladder (by age 30) and the OECD social and emotional skills scales. The outcome is a 1–10 expected relative decile on a MacArthur-type social status ladder, while key predictors include ESCS-based objective social status deciles, seven social and emotional skills (perseverance, emotional control, stress resistance, empathy, cooperation, curiosity, assertiveness), and mathematics achievement quintiles derived from PISA mathematics plausible values. Missing data were addressed with multiple imputation via chained equations (10 datasets) and estimates were combined using Rubin’s rule; standard errors incorporate PISA complex sampling using final weights and BRR replicate weights. The paper reports path coefficients and mediation decompositions rather than ML predictive performance metrics, and it emphasizes that associations are correlational, so causal claims about mediation cannot be made.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 (15-year-olds) Expected relative social status by age 30 (social status ladder)
all_target_variables: Expected relative social status (ERSS) at age 30 (1–10 ladder)

title: Decoding divides: The role of socioeconomic status and personality traits in AI divides and educational inequality
authors: Zeyu Wang, Sanne van Wetten, Eliane Segers, Carla Haelermans
outcome_summary: The study analyzes mediation pathways linking family SES and personality traits (openness, extraversion, perseverance) to Grade 6 academic performance in the Netherlands using Education Monitor Limburg (OML) 2022–2023 data linked to national registry exit test scores (final analytic sample N=4,497). Academic performance was operationalized as within-test-provider national percentiles to align heterogeneous test scales, and the two mediators were AI usage intensity and digital literacy. AI usage intensity was constructed using a CatBoost model that predicts students’ self-reported digital tool usage frequency from teacher-reported tool-context indicators, while digital literacy and personality traits were scaled using GRM-based IRT composites. In parallel mediation (PROCESS Model 4), digital literacy showed a significant positive association with performance (B=1.78, SE=0.37, 95% CI [1.06, 2.51]) and produced significant indirect effects for all three personality traits, whereas AI usage intensity showed no significant mediation. The study uses OLS with school-cluster robust SEs and listwise deletion for missingness; it is cross-sectional, so mediation is correlational rather than causal.
all_datasets_used: OML 2022–2023 Netherlands Grade 6 academic performance (exit test score percentiles)

title: Uncovering student profiles. An explainable cluster analysis approach to PISA 2022
authors: Miguel Alvarez-Garcia, Mar Arenas-Parra, Raquel Ibar-Alonso
outcome_summary: The study applies an explainable cluster analysis pipeline to PISA 2022 Spanish student data (15-year-olds), using the full sample (n = 30,800) and 74 student-context variables transformed into 16 derived variables. It performs k-means clustering to obtain an optimal solution of 7 student clusters, then compares classification pipelines to label/interpret clusters, using SHAP for global and local interpretability. The best-performing classification model reaches global accuracy of 0.8643 on the test set, with precision ranging from 0.8401 to 0.9321 and recall from 0.8055 to 0.9406. The most predictive features for cluster categorization are ESCS and ICT use at home and school, and the authors report cluster differences in gender patterns, academic performance, and educational expectations. A key limitation is that the paper does not document the missing-data handling strategy, and SHAP-based feature importance supports prediction interpretability rather than causal claims.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 (Spain) student data (15-year-olds), clustering + cluster classification

title: Beyond the test scores: Balancing information and accountability in global assessment systems
authors: Yuan Cui, Qian Zhao, Kit-Tai Hau
outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2022 mathematics data for 15-year-old students from 65 economies (479,178 students; 17,783 schools) and models mathematics achievement using a three-level hierarchical linear model with ten mathematics plausible values combined via Rubin’s rules. It estimates how two economy-level policy instruments—test frequency (principal-reported) and test-based accountability (STDTEST)—relate to achievement, net of student (gender, ESCS, immigration), school (school ESCS, student–teacher ratio, school type), and economy (log GDP) controls. In the main specification, test-based accountability shows a negative association with achievement (β≈-0.13, p<.01) while test frequency shows a positive association (β≈0.15, p<.01), and the accountability×frequency interaction is not significant. Cross-level moderation indicates accountability is more harmful in higher-SES contexts and frequency is more beneficial for lower-SES contexts, with no significant moderation by GDP. Limitations include cross-sectional inference and incomplete reporting of missing-data handling at the student level.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (15-year-olds), economy-level policy instruments | PISA 2022 Mathematics (15-year-olds), cross-level moderation by SES and GDP

title: Evaluating the effects of ICT engagement on science and mathematics achievement: Evidence from PISA 2022 using structural equation modeling
authors: F. Ornek, E. Afari
outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 Türkiye (n=7250; 15-year-olds) using student questionnaire measures of ICT engagement and OECD-provided plausible values for mathematics and science (PV1MATH–PV10MATH; PV1SCIE–PV10SCIE). The authors estimate a theory-driven mediation and non-linear model with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4, using bootstrapping (5000 resamples) and reporting path coefficients, effect sizes (f2), and predictive relevance (Q2). For mathematics, ICTHOME and ICTEFFIC show significant positive linear effects, while leisure ICT use (ICTWKDY) is significantly negative; ICTOUT’s linear effect is not significant, but mediation via ICTEFFIC is significant (indirect effect=0.069, t=6.54***). For science, ICTHOME, ICTOUT, and ICTEFFIC are positive, while ICTWKDY is negative, with significant quadratic terms indicating changing returns across ICT intensity. Limitations include cross-sectional data (no causal identification) and incomplete reporting of missing-data handling for questionnaire indicators.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Türkiye (15-year-olds) Mathematics achievement (PV1MATH–PV10MATH) | PISA 2022 Türkiye (15-year-olds) Science achievement (PV1SCIE–PV10SCIE)

title: Gender, mindset, and teacher support predict students’ math motivation profiles: Evidence from five countries in PISA 2022
outcome_summary: This study used PISA 2022 student microdata for 15-year-olds in Finland, Germany, Japan, Korea, and the United States (total N=27,421) to identify math motivation latent profiles based on WLE-scaled indicators of self-efficacy, anxiety, intrinsic value, and attainment value. The authors estimated latent profile models in Mplus (MLR with robust SEs and FIML for missingness) and then compared profile means for four math outcomes: classroom engagement, math homework time, STEM career intention, and math achievement. Achievement contrasts were computed using 10 plausible values with multiple imputations, and profile differences were tested with Wald tests (Bonferroni-corrected p < .003). The highly motivated profile consistently showed the most favorable outcomes, while unmotivated profiles showed the least favorable outcomes, with cross-national exceptions for the mixed profile. Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal inference) and reliance on single-item measures for intrinsic and attainment value.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 (15-year-olds) Mathematics motivation profiles (WLE indicators) — Finland, Germany, Japan, Korea, United States

title: Understanding the relationships among ICT use, self-efficacy, and achievement in PISA 2022: A multigroup analysis featuring gender and immigrant status
authors: Mitcho Hristov, Takumi Yada, Janne Fagerlund, Piia N¨aykki, P¨aivi H¨akkinen
outcome_summary: This study analyzes Finnish PISA 2022 data (N=10,239 overall; immigrant-status groups Ntotal=9,874) to examine how ICT use and self-efficacy in digital competencies relate to achievement in math, reading, and science. The authors operationalize ICT use for learning (IC174) and ICT use for leisure (IC177), and split self-efficacy in digital competencies (IC183) into two latent factors: CIL (11 items) and CT (3 items). Using SEM in Mplus with Fay’s balanced repeated replication (BRR) and 10 plausible values per subject, they report acceptable model fit (overall: RMSEA=.043, CFI=.930, TLI=.921, SRMR=.065). Across subjects, ICT use for learning shows no significant direct effect but a positive total effect via mediation through CIL self-efficacy, whereas ICT use for leisure is negatively associated with achievement. The immigrant-status multigroup results suggest that CIL self-efficacy can be protective for immigrant students, but the paper does not fully document a general missing-data strategy beyond the immigrant-status derivation rule.

all_target_variables: Math achievement (Plausible Values) | Reading achievement (Plausible Values) | Science achievement (Plausible Values) | Math achievement (Plausible Values) — girls vs boys

title: Profiles of academic performance and perceived digital distraction in secondary classrooms
authors: Chenyang Li, Fu Chen
outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 microdata for 15-year-old students from 30 education systems (N=239,695; 8,826 schools) with mathematics as the major domain. Mathematics achievement is represented by ten plausible values (PV1MATH–PV10MATH), and digital distraction is measured using the single PISA item ST273Q06 with reverse coding and school-level group-mean centering to form DIGDIST_L1. After MICE-based iterative imputation (LightGBM estimators), the authors identify four student profiles via a weighted cluster ensemble (k=4) and then classify profile membership using XGBoost with SMOTE-Tomek inside a stratified 5-fold cross-validation pipeline. Across five pairwise comparisons, XGBoost achieves high discrimination (Accuracy 0.804–0.946; AUC 0.898–0.984; F1 0.769–0.911). SHAP is used for interpretation, but feature importance is not causal; additionally, the paper does not indicate design-weighted training for the ML models, so predictive performance should be interpreted as classification accuracy rather than population-level effects.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (15-year-olds; PV1MATH–PV10MATH; school-level centered digital distraction)
all_target_variables: Profile membership: Clu_2 (High-Distraction Low-Achievers) vs Clu_1 (Low-Distraction High-Achievers)

title: Mind the gap: Uncovering student’s learning achievement disparities in Cambodian urban and rural secondary schools
authors: R. Minami, K. Ogawa
outcome_summary: The study uses Cambodia’s PISA 2022 microdata (public secondary school students) and analyzes mathematics and reading achievement across the 10th–90th percentiles using unconditional quantile regression (UQR), with school-cluster adjusted standard errors to reflect PISA’s two-stage sampling. It then applies a Recentered Influence Function (RIF) Oaxaca–Blinder decomposition to quantify how much of the urban–rural achievement gap is attributable to tangible (explained) versus intangible (unexplained) components. The results show that rural schooling is associated with lower achievement across the distribution, with stronger disadvantages for low-performing students, and that student-related factors (e.g., gender, ECE, waged labor, SES, phone use) generally matter more than school-level variables. Decomposition results indicate intangible factors dominate the gap among low achievers (mathematics: 61.3% at the 10th percentile; reading: 73.1% at the 10th percentile) but decline toward higher percentiles. Limitations include the absence of reported survey-weight usage and missing-data handling, and the fact that decomposition/unconditional quantile regression are not causal identification strategies.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Cambodia (public secondary students) — Mathematics achievement | PISA 2022 Cambodia (public secondary students) — Reading achievement
all_target_variables: Urban–rural achievement gap explained by tangible vs intangible factors (RIF-Oaxaca–Blinder decomposition)

title: 1-s2.0-S0738059324001974-main
authors: J. Liu, Amin Abdul, Millicent Aziku, Yue Chen
outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 Vietnam mathematics data for 15-year-old students (final N=5711) to test a mediation framework linking inquiry-based pedagogy (IBP) to student math attitude (SMA) and then to math performance (SMP). Math performance is modeled as a latent construct based on ten plausible values, while IBP and SMA are latent constructs from student questionnaire Likert items. Using a PLS-SEM mediation model estimated in STATA, the authors report good overall fit (CFI=0.97, TLI=0.96, RMSEA=0.052, SRMR=0.058) and significant standardized paths: IBP→SMA (std.β=0.424, p<0.001), SMA→SMP (std.β=0.072, p<0.001), IBP→SMP (std.β=0.084, p<0.001), and the indirect mediation IBP→SMA→SMP (std.β=0.030, p<0.001). The paper uses listwise deletion for missing IBP/SMA responses and does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights, and the cross-sectional SEM design constrains causal claims.

title: Overworked and under-creative: Teacher workload, time allocation, and creative pedagogy in Chinese secondary schools - evidence from PISA 2022
authors: Y. Wang
outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2022 teacher and principal survey data for Hong Kong and Macao to explain how teacher workload composition and time allocation relate to teachers’ prioritization of creative pedagogies (CREATEDPED), with ICT use as a moderator. The dependent variable is an IRT-transformed synthetic scale from 7 Likert items, and teacher-level measures are aggregated to the school level using CNTSCHID. Results from hierarchical linear modeling and OLS with school fixed effects show that overall weekly workload is not significantly correlated with creative pedagogy, while teaching-related time allocation exhibits a U-shaped pattern at the teacher level and an inverted U-shaped pattern at the school level (peak around ~60% teaching-related time). ICT use is positively associated with creative pedagogy and moderates the relationship between time allocation/workload and creative pedagogy. Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal inference) and incomplete reporting of missing-data handling and exact survey-weight implementation.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Teacher & Principal Survey (Hong Kong & Macao) — creative pedagogy scale (CREATEDPED)

title: Socioeconomic achievement gap in Taiwan: The impact of COVID-19 on math performance
authors: Tzung-Ruei Tsou
outcome_summary: This study analyzes OECD PISA Taiwan data for math achievement across six cycles (2006, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2022), focusing on students in the bottom vs top quarter of ESCS to define lower- and higher-SES groups. Using a difference-in-differences design with year fixed effects and controls (grade, gender, immigrant background, setting, public/private, and general/vocational), the paper finds that the SES math gap widened in 2022: in the fully specified DID model, the Lower×Post interaction is β = -26.110 (s.e. 7.928), p < 0.01, corresponding to roughly a one-year learning loss magnitude per OECD scaling. Descriptively, lower-SES students declined by about 10 points from pre- to post-pandemic, while higher-SES students increased by about 7.6 points. The analysis is not an ML predictive modeling study (no ML algorithms are trained), and the manuscript does not report how plausible values were combined or how missing data were handled, limiting full transparency of inference.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2006–2022 Taiwan (secondary students), Math achievement (Plausible Values)
all_target_variables: Math achievement gap (Lower × Post DID interaction)

title: Optimal class size and learning outcomes in Morocco: A normative-causal approach using PISA 2022 data
authors: Lagdiri Youness, Ouazzanitouhami Naoual
outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 microdata for Morocco, restricted to 150 public lower secondary schools and 5962 sampled 15-year-olds. It combines a normative multi-criteria optimization model (pedagogical performance from PV-based spline regressions with ESCS controls plus an economic cost function calibrated to Moroccan budget realities) with a simulated fuzzy regression discontinuity design (FRDD) for causal validation. Plausible values are handled using Rubin’s (1987) rules, and the analysis applies the student sampling weight W_FSTUWT throughout. The optimization identifies a global optimum class size of 23.4 students (95% CI: [23.35, 23.36]) with domain optima of 22.2 (reading) to 24.3 (mathematics), requiring a +49.3% per-student cost increase and yielding +25.1 PISA points (ROI = 29.1, “Good”). FRDD results show a “high-performance corridor” at 23–26 students with positive LATEs and significant deterioration beyond 30 for composite indices. Limitations include the simulated nature of the FRDD treatment assignment (instrument strength is only moderate) and missing-data handling is not reported.

title: Understanding the relationship between teacher collaboration beliefs and job satisfaction via collaborative attitudes: A moderated mediation model of classroom self-efficacy from PISA 2022
authors: Yang Zhang, Denis Djekourmane, Yiheng Qin
outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 teacher questionnaire data from 40,349 teachers and schools across 17 countries/economies (including ARE, PRT, DEU, KOR, and others). The analysis is a moderated mediation framework: teacher collaboration beliefs predict teacher collaborative attitudes, which in turn predict teacher job satisfaction, with classroom self-efficacy and gender moderating key pathways. Missing data were handled via pairwise deletion, and the constructs were validated using CFA before estimating the structural relations. The results show a significant positive direct effect of collaboration beliefs on collaborative attitudes (β = 0.162, p < 0.001), no significant direct effect of collaboration beliefs on job satisfaction (β = 0.002, p > 0.646), but a significant indirect effect through collaborative attitudes (β = 0.012, p < 0.001) and a significant direct effect of collaborative attitudes on job satisfaction (β = 0.073, p < 0.001). Because the design is cross-sectional and the manuscript does not document the use of PISA teacher sampling weights, causal claims and population-representativeness precision should be interpreted cautiously.
all_target_variables: Teacher collaborative attitudes | Teacher job satisfaction | Moderated mediation pathways to Teacher job satisfaction

title: 1-s2.0-S0883035525001727-main
authors: Chunjin Chen, Hongbiao Yin
outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2022 Teacher Questionnaire teacher-level data from 15 countries/regions (total N=46,563; 3628 schools), focusing on how perceived instructional leadership relates to teacher well-being through teacher workload stress, with teacher autonomy support as a moderator. The authors estimate a moderated mediation model in Stata 18.0 using SEM and report acceptable model fit across economies (CFI>0.90, TLI>0.90, RMSEA<0.06, SRMR<0.05), with balanced repeated replication (BRR) used for sampling-error estimation. In the total sample, instructional leadership shows a positive direct effect on well-being (standardized 0.278***), while workload stress negatively predicts well-being (−0.428***), yielding a positive indirect effect of instructional leadership via workload stress (0.061***). The autonomy support main effect is positive (0.197***), and the interaction AUTO*LOAD→WELL is significant (0.040***), indicating buffering of workload stress. Limitations include cross-sectional data (no causal inference) and missing-data handling for questionnaire items not being explicitly reported.

title: Pathways to equity: A mediation analysis of gender, SES, and mathematics achievement using PISA 2022 UK data
authors: Mengying Huang, Xin Liu
outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 mathematics data for the United Kingdom (12,972 students from 451 schools) to test a mediation/path model linking gender and ESCS to mathematics achievement through mathematics teacher support, growth mindset, and mathematics anxiety. Mathematics achievement is measured using 10 plausible values (PV1MATH–PV10MATH) and estimated in Mplus with TYPE=IMPUTATION averaging across plausible-value datasets. In direct effects, ESCS positively predicted achievement (β=0.30, p<0.05), while mathematics anxiety showed the largest negative association (β=-0.24, p<0.05); growth mindset was positive (β=0.12, p<0.05) and teacher support was weakly positive (β=0.03, p<0.05). Gender had no significant direct effect on achievement (β=-0.00, p=0.93). The model fit was reported as CFI=1.00, RMSEA=0.00, SRMR=0.00, but the paper does not report a missing-data handling strategy for questionnaire/scale variables and does not document whether PISA complex-survey weights were applied, limiting generalizability and interpretability of mediation as causal.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (UK, 15-year-olds) — mathematics achievement (PVMATH plausible values)

title: Being female and being well-situated implies higher performance on creative thinking tests: Evidence across 62 countries from PISA 2022
authors: B. Goecke, M. Benedek, J.G. Diedrich, B. Forthmann, S. Patzl, S. Weiss
outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 microdata for 62 countries/economies (N=493,660 students) using an integrative two-stage individual-participant meta-analytic approach. It estimates country-specific regression effects on PISA plausible values for creative thinking (innovative domain), mathematics, and reading, then meta-analyzes the standardized coefficients using cluster-robust random-effects models with BRR/Fay replicate-weight variance estimation. Missing ESCS values are handled via nested multiple imputation (M=10) compatible with the subsequent effect-size regressions, and PVs are combined using Rubin’s rules. Across domains, female students outperform male students in creative thinking and reading (e.g., creative thinking gender estimate = -0.277, p<0.001), while SES shows strong positive associations with performance (creative thinking SES estimate = 0.334, p<0.001). The paper reports heterogeneity (e.g., high I² for gender effects) and tests macro moderators (OECD membership, HDI, GGGI, power distance), finding creative-thinking disparities largely stable across contexts. Limitations include reliance on observational cross-sectional PISA data and the fact that the approach is not ML predictive modeling despite ML-related framing in the venue.

all_target_variables: Creative thinking (PVs) — gender main effect (Gender coded 0=female, 1=male) | Mathematics (PVs) — gender main effect (Gender coded 0=female, 1=male) | Reading (PVs) — gender main effect (Gender coded 0=female, 1=male)

title: Creative learning environments and mathematics self-efficacy as predictors of mathematics achievement: Insights from PISA 2022 across three countries – Korea, Canada, and Türkiye
authors: S. Ö. Bütüner, Pınar Güner, Mustafa Güler
outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 mathematics data for 15-year-old students in Korea (n=6454), Canada (n=23073), and Türkiye (n=7250) to test a structural equation model linking creative learning environments to mathematics achievement through mathematics self-efficacy (MATHEF21). Mathematics achievement is modeled using PISA plausible values PV1MATH–PV10MATH, and the authors report path coefficients with bootstrap confidence intervals. The model shows that both creative peers/family and creative school/class environments positively predict MATHEF21 across all three countries, with MATHEF21 explaining a moderate share of achievement variance (MATHEF21→MATHACH β≈0.31–0.52). For achievement, creative peers/family has small positive direct effects, while creative school/class has small negative direct effects, but both creative environments have positive indirect effects via MATHEF21. Limitations include the cross-sectional design (associational not causal) and unclear use of PISA sampling weights/replicate weights.

title: Separating prior knowledge from acquired knowledge: An individual differences analysis of PISA - learning in the digital world
authors: Leonard Tetzlaff, Lothar Persic-Beck, Ulf Kröhne, Carolin Hahnel, Daniel Schiffner, Frank Goldhammer
outcome_summary: This study analyzes a German add-on to PISA 2022 using the innovative PISA 2025 domain “Learning in the digital world (LDW)”. Students completed two LDW units (system modelling and block-based programming), each with a pretest (binary items) followed by learning-centre tasks with worked examples, and a Big Challenge (BC) task; the outcome was an EAP ability estimate from the BC, with a residual constructed by regressing BC on pretest to approximate “acquired knowledge”. The authors used model-based residual estimation (FIML for missingness) and cluster-robust standard errors for students nested in schools; no ML algorithms were trained. They report that after controlling for prior knowledge, 21% residual variance remained, which was significantly explained by worked-example use (β=0.63, p≤0.01) and general intelligence (β=0.73, p≤0.01), jointly explaining 93% of residual variance. Controlling for complex problem solving reduced residual variance to 13% and attenuated intelligence (β=0.23, p≤0.01). Mastery orientation had an indirect effect on the residual mediated fully by worked-example use (indirect β=0.22, p=.01). Limitations include the lack of experimental manipulation and the interpretation of residuals as learning differences rather than causal learning effects.

title: The effects of teaching initiative, ICT application, and teaching collaboration on teachers’ creative thinking: Latent profile and multiple logistic regression analysis
outcome_summary: This study analyzed PISA 2022 Teacher Questionnaire (International Option) data restricted to teachers in Hong Kong and Macao Special Administrative Regions (final N=4069; HKG=2165, MAC=1904). Teachers’ creative thinking was operationalized as three WLE-scaled dimensions (openness to creativity, creative values, creative pedagogies) and classified via Latent Profile Analysis, yielding an optimal 5-class solution (C-5) with entropy=0.93 and significant BLRT/LMRT (p<.001). Multiple logistic regression then explained membership in each creative-thinking class (reference: Class 1) using Gender, Age, Region, Subject, Teaching initiative, ICT application, and Teaching collaboration, with key gradient effects: Teaching initiative OR=1.397/1.526/1.893 for Classes 3/4/5 (p<.001), ICT application OR=1.148/1.336/1.524/1.726 for Classes 2–5 (p<.05 to p<.001), and Teaching collaboration OR=1.211/1.266/1.613 for Classes 3–5 (p<.05 to p<.001). The paper uses WLE (not PVs) and handles missingness via FIML in Mplus with TYPE=COMPLEX for school clustering; however, the design is cross-sectional and correlational, so reverse causality and response bias remain plausible limitations.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Teacher Questionnaire (International Option) — Hong Kong & Macao teachers
all_target_variables: Teachers’ creative thinking class membership (5-class LPA outcome)

title: Mapping student engagement in creative thinking: An explainable machine learning approach to behavioral heterogeneity
authors: Qin Wang, Fu Chen, Yu Han, Xiaofei Li, Chang Lu
outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 creative thinking computer-based assessment (CBA) process data and student questionnaire context for three economies (Canada, Germany, Hong Kong; total valid creative-thinking test cases: Canada n=6,794, Germany n=1,692, Hong Kong n=1,661). It first identifies disengaged behaviors (rapid responding, relative rapid responding, non-responding) and uses k-means clustering on four process features (credits, action count, orientation time, processing time) to derive six engagement patterns across tasks. For prediction, students are labeled as engaged vs disengaged based on their most common pattern across multiple creative tasks, and contextual variables are merged; variables with >30% missingness are deleted and remaining missing values are imputed via hot-deck KNN. Using LASSO for feature selection and XGBoost for classification (with SMOTE and class weighting to address ~95/5 imbalance), the models achieve Accuracy/F1 of 0.92/0.93 (Canada), 0.91/0.92 (Germany), and 0.87/0.87 (Hong Kong), with SHAP used for global explainability. Limitations include the lack of reported survey-weight usage and the fact that SHAP explanations support predictive interpretation rather than causal claims.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (CBA) — Canada | PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (CBA) — Germany | PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (CBA) — Hong Kong

title: Cross-cultural differential item functioning in the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment
authors: Jiayi Cen, Christian Bokhove, Nora McIntyre
outcome_summary: This open-access journal article analyzes cross-cultural differential item functioning in the OECD PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (CT) assessment for 15-year-olds, using secondary PISA 2022 international database microdata. The authors include 137,851 students from 63 participating countries/economies and calibrate an IRT-based DFIT framework across ten extended GLOBE cultural clusters, using the Anglo cluster as the reference group. Across 30 retained CT items, 83.3% were flagged for DIF above a practical threshold (NCDIF > 0.0115), with the largest effects reported for DT360Q01C2 (Max NCDIF = 0.188) and DT500Q01C (Max NCDIF = 0.176). Cluster-level aggregation shows systematic disadvantage for some clusters (e.g., Sub-Saharan Africa net mean SA = −0.690; DTF = 1.668) and net advantage for others (e.g., Confucian Asia net mean SA = 0.338; DTF = 3.944). The study does not report PV handling or a missing-data strategy for PVs because the DIF analysis is IRT-based on item responses; survey-weight use is also not explicitly documented, so population-representativeness of DIF indices should be interpreted cautiously.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (CT) Grade 10/15-year-olds, cross-cultural DIF (IRT-DFIT) across cultural clusters | PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (CT) Grade 10/15-year-olds, qualitative diagnosis of DIF items
all_target_variables: Item-level differential functioning (NCDIF; DIF flagging across cultural clusters) | Mechanisms explaining DIF (four interpretive dimensions applied to high-impact items)

title: Balancing creativity and emotional health: The role of openness
authors: M.D. Wang, Suzannie Kit-Ying Leung, Jenny Wanyi Li
outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment data for 15-year-olds (N=613,744 overall) and links it to optional emotional-health modules: emotional control (430,289 students across 61 economies), stress resistance (292,466 across 42), and psychosomatic symptoms (112,798 across 14). The authors estimate multilevel regression models with students nested within schools and countries, pooling results across 10 plausible values and 10 multiple-imputed datasets (fully conditional specification with predictive mean matching; five donors). They incorporate the PISA student weight W_FSTUWT to preserve representativeness and use standardized coefficients (β). Across outcomes, creative thinking test scores show significant quadratic effects for emotional control, stress resistance, and psychosomatic symptoms, consistent with a U-shaped pattern for psychosomatic symptoms. Openness to intellect is generally protective (higher emotional control/stress resistance, lower psychosomatic symptoms), whereas openness to art is a risk factor (lower emotional regulation and higher psychosomatic symptoms), with moderation by gender and individualism. Limitations include cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report emotional health measures, so causal interpretations are not warranted.

all_target_variables: Emotional control (index) | Stress resistance (index) | Psychosomatic symptoms (index)

title: Exploring the relationship between reading literacy and creativity competence: A multilevel modeling approach
authors: Y. Cai, Yan Chen, Yan Yang
outcome_summary: The study analyzes the Hong Kong sample of OECD PISA 2022 (15-year-olds; 5557 students nested in 163 schools) to examine how reading literacy relates to creativity competence at both student and school levels. Reading literacy and creativity competence are both represented using PISA plausible values, with the authors using all 10 plausible values and reporting average statistics; multilevel path modeling in Mplus is used to account for nesting. The model fit is reported as excellent (χ2/df = 0.046/1, RMSEA = 0.000, CFI = 1.000, TLI = 1.000, SRMR within/between = 0.001/0.000). At the student level, reading literacy strongly predicts creativity (β = 0.44, p < .01), while SES has a small positive effect (β = 0.04, p < .01) and gender shows males scoring lower (β = −0.12, p < .01). At the school level, school mean reading literacy is the strongest predictor of school creativity (β = 0.74, p < .01), with school SES also significant (β = 0.31, p < .01). Limitations include the cross-sectional nature (no causal claims) and unclear use of PISA sampling weights.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 Hong Kong (15-year-olds) Reading literacy → Creativity competence (overall score; 10 PVs) | PISA 2022 Hong Kong (15-year-olds) School mean reading literacy → School creativity (overall score; 10 PVs aggregated)

title: Solving the paradox between the generalized partial credit model and PISA’s rating instructions: A generalized IRTree approach to within-rating multidimensionality
authors: Nils Myszkowski, Martin Storme
outcome_summary: This paper re-analyzed PISA 2022 Creative Thinking rater-mediated trichotomous scores (no credit/partial/full) at the item-response level, focusing on whether the generalized partial credit model’s within-rating unidimensionality assumption is consistent with OECD rating instructions. The authors excluded binary-scored items and recoded each ordinal item into two sequential node decisions, then estimated generalized item response tree (IRTree) models: a within-rating unidimensional baseline (Tutz sequential model) and within-rating multidimensional specifications aligned to the scoring rubric (appropriateness at node 1; originality/diversity at node 2, conditional on passing node 1). Model fit comparisons used AIC, BIC, SABIC, and HQ, with multidimensional models outperforming unidimensional ones for EII and GCI and showing an overall better fit pattern across subtests. Reliability was lower for node-2 traits (originality/diversity) than for node-1 traits (appropriateness), and latent traits correlated strongly with each other and with PISA mathematics, reading, and science performance. Limitations include the lack of reported survey-weight usage and the fact that the study evaluates measurement-model assumptions rather than PV-based score validity directly.

title: Navigating the impact of the pandemic on teacher competencies: A comparative analysis across economic contexts using pre- and post-COVID-19 PISA data
authors: D.R. Joshi, Jeevan Khanal, Krishna Prasad Sharma Chapai
outcome_summary: This open-access study uses PISA teacher questionnaire data from 2019 (pre-COVID; CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ) and 2023 (post-COVID) merged with CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ, covering 128,866 teachers across 24 countries grouped into LMICs, UMICs, and HICs. The analysis compares pre/post means and economic-level differences for six constructs (empowerment, management, adaptability, professionalism needs, inclusion needs, and collaboration) and reports SEM model fit (RMSEA=0.02; NFI=0.91; CFI=0.91; TLI=0.90). Key results show empowerment (3.23→3.36, p=0.00), management (3.30→3.40, p=0.00), adaptability (3.33→3.39, p=0.00), and collaboration (4.42→4.51, p=0.00) increasing post-COVID, while professionalism needs slightly decline (2.83→2.81, p=0.00) and inclusion needs rise (2.55→2.62, p=0.00). Professional development needs and collaboration are modeled as positively associated with competencies (e.g., collaboration Beta=0.31 in text). Limitations include reliance on self-reported measures, unclear missing-data handling, and cross-sectional pre/post design that restricts causal claims about COVID-19.

title: 1-s2.0-S2530380524000157-main
authors: Pablo Javier Ortega-Rodríguez
outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2022 Spain student data (ages 15–16) using a three-level hierarchical model (students nested in schools and autonomous communities). The final analytic sample comprises 28,792 students from 935 schools, after excluding 2,008 students with incomplete information; missingness was assessed as MCAR and handled via listwise deletion. Mathematics competence is measured on the PISA mathematics scale (mean 500, SD 100) and the study uses ten plausible values, averaging them to obtain the dependent score. The multilevel results show that gender differences are statistically significant, mathematics anxiety is negatively associated with performance (η²=0.063, medium effect), and mathematics self-efficacy is positively associated (η²=0.012, small effect), alongside positive associations for socioeconomic context and family cultural capital. The manuscript does not report the use of PISA sampling/replicate weights, so population-representativeness and standard error calibration may be limited; additionally, the design is ex post facto, so causal claims cannot be inferred.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 (Spain) Grade 15-16 Mathematics competence (Rasch scale; PVs averaged)

title: 1-s2.0-S1871187126001100-main
outcome_summary: The study analyzed PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (CT) item responses from Form 37 (15 items) administered to 10,779 students across all countries that used Form 37. It applied the PCtree (partial credit tree) model to recursively partition students using demographic covariates (gender, ESCS, immigrant background), producing six terminal subgroups and indicating violations of measurement invariance. To identify item-level DIF responsible for these partitions, the authors ran logistic ordinal regression DIF tests for all pairwise subgroup comparisons (225 models across 15 items), detecting DIF in 122 comparisons. Although DIF was detected in nearly half of the pairwise tests and all items showed DIF in more than one comparison, effect sizes were negligible (ΔR2 ranged 0 to 0.028). The analysis is limited to one form (Form 37) and uses deletion of missing covariate values; additionally, the study does not report whether PISA sampling weights were applied, which affects how confidently these DIF patterns generalize.

title: Subjective well-being and educational performance in PISA: A copula based approach
authors: B. Tong
outcome_summary: The paper analyzes PISA 2022 (15-year-olds) using a copula-based approach to study the dependence between overall educational performance and a latent subjective well-being (SWB) construct. The SWB construct is built from a factor analysis using ST016 life satisfaction plus well-being questionnaire items (WB155Q01, WB155Q08, WB155Q10), and the authors restrict the sample to the 13 countries/economies that administered the additional well-being questionnaire. For performance, they merge PV1READ, PV1MATH, and PV1SCIE by averaging them and they use only one plausible value. Across five copula families, the CIC criterion selects the Gaussian copula, yielding a very small dependence parameter (θ=0.005) and a weak Pearson correlation (r=0.026). A robustness check using WLS with W_FSTUWT in IEA IDB Analyzer reports small coefficients and low explanatory power (R2=0.030), but the copula section does not document missing-data handling or hierarchical dependence adjustments, limiting causal interpretation and reproducibility.
all_datasets_used: PISA 2022 (15-year-olds) — overall performance (mean of PV1READ, PV1MATH, PV1SCIE) and latent SWB factor score from ST016 + WB155Q01/WB155Q08/WB155Q10
all_target_variables: Dependence between PISA performance and SWB construct (copula dependence; Gaussian copula parameter)

title: The impact of financial education in schools on the financial literacy of Brazilian students
authors: Natali Morgana Cassola, Kalinca Léia Becker, Kelmara Mendes Vieira
outcome_summary: This study estimates the impact of school-based financial education on financial literacy using PISA 2022 Financial Literacy microdata for Brazil (final analytic sample N=3458). The dependent variable is PVFL, constructed as a weighted average of the ten plausible values, and the main identification strategy is Propensity Score Matching (nearest neighbor with five neighbors) combined with quantile regression (UQTE). After matching, exposure to financial education topics at school is associated with an average increase of +45.57 PVFL points (SE=3.85; 95% CI [38.02; 53.14]), and the effect is robust to Rosenbaum sensitivity up to γ=2.0. Topic-specific results show the largest gains for Financial Planning (+49.99) and Credit & Debt (+42.88), with heterogeneous effects across the PVFL distribution. Limitations include cross-sectional measurement of exposure via student self-reports and reliance on PSM/ignorability assumptions rather than randomized treatment; the paper also does not use ML algorithms, so “ML” performance metrics are not applicable.

title: Creative thinking, mathematics achievement, and well-being: A multilevel analysis of Spanish students
outcome_summary: This study uses OECD PISA 2022 microdata for Spain (15-year-olds; 30,800 students in 966 schools) to examine how creativity-related factors relate to mathematics achievement and well-being using two-level multilevel linear models. Mathematics achievement is modeled with PV1MATH (first plausible value), while life satisfaction (LIFE-SAT) and stress resistance (STRESAGR) are modeled using WLE questionnaire scales. The key results show that creative thinking performance strongly predicts mathematics achievement (β=3.95, p<.001) and that school-average creative thinking remains significant after student controls (β=2.54, p<.001), whereas the Creative Thinking × SES interaction is not significant (β=0.01, p=.691). For well-being, creative self-efficacy is the consistent positive predictor (life satisfaction β=0.16, p<.001; stress resistance β=0.10, p<.001), while creative thinking has a small negative association with life satisfaction (β=-0.03, p<.001) and is not significant for stress resistance. Limitations include cross-sectional associations and primary analyses using only the first plausible value, plus the paper’s explicit use of MICE for a rotationally missing school variable but no reported design-weight application.

title: The impact of digital resource utilization on student learning outcomes and self-efficacy across different economic contexts: A comparative analysis of PISA, 2022
authors: Dirgha Raj Joshi, Jeevan Khanal, Krishna Prasad Sharma Chapai, Krishna Prasad Adhikari
outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2022 questionnaire data across 50 countries (237,844 students after cleaning missing cases) and groups countries into IMF GDP-per-capita income categories (low middle-income, middle-income, high-income). It constructs six digital-resource/self-efficacy constructs (UAS, UOS, USL, USF, USA, SEC) from 37 retained PISA items and validates the measurement model using CFA, then tests a hypothesized structural model using multi-group SEM and ANOVA. The SEM model fit is reported as good (RMSEA=0.04; GFI=0.90; NFI=0.92; CFI=0.92; TLI=0.91; SRMR=0.03). Key results show UOS as the strongest positive predictor of SEC, USA as the strongest positive predictor of USF, and USF/USA/UAS as positive predictors of USL (with UOS often negative). Limitations include the absence of reported survey-weight usage and the fact that the study does not use PV-based achievement outcomes, so findings concern digital engagement/self-efficacy constructs rather than test-score effects.
